title: Normalize inline validation timing, soft-error states, and token signals for responsive inputs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Our current form controls show inconsistent inline validation timing (on-blur vs on-type) and visual "soft-error" states across desktop and mobile. This produces UX parity bugs: fields that validate immediately on mobile but wait until blur on desktop, inconsistent color/opacity usages for soft vs hard errors, and ambiguous token mappings for focus/invalid/assistive states. Outcome: A clear, platform-consistent approach to validation timing and a set of token-driven soft-error states so engineers can implement reliably across runtime variants (hosted, dedicated, private) and across device sizes.
background: Over the last year we've accumulated ad-hoc validation behaviors while shipping feature work (console forms, signup, billing UI). Designers and engineers have implemented localized fixes rather than a system-level contract. This has created customer-facing regressions (support tickets about validation oddities) and brittle CSS/JS guardrails. Relevant incidents: support-1128 (confusing validation on small screens).
scope: In-scope: text inputs, textarea, select (single), toggle/switch, and form-level error summary anchor behavior. Define timing heuristics (on-type debounce, on-blur final validation), soft-error visual token values, screen-reader announcement rules, and mobile touch target considerations. Out-of-scope: multi-select chips, experimental autosuggest rewrite, and server-side validation APIs (PM/ENG will own contract).
success_metrics: 1) Reduce validation-related support tickets by 30% in next quarter. 2) Consistent WCAG announcement behavior across desktop/mobile (QA checklist). 3) All core form components consume new tokens and pass visual regression tests in console-2026.03 release.
acceptance_criteria:
- Design spec exported to Figma with component states (idle, focus, soft-error, hard-error, success) for desktop and mobile.
- Token sheet with color, opacity, motion-duration, and spacing values.
- A11y notes: SR announce priority, role=alert usage for form-level summary, avoid double announcements.
- Frontend acceptance: ENG-3382 implements tokens and timing; QA passes on staging.
- Automated Storybook stories cover timing flows and can be snapshot-tested.

comments: 2026-02-22 - Ava M: Initial discovery complete. Collected examples from Console, Signup, and Billing flows. Noted three inconsistent patterns: (1) on-type live validation for short text fields, (2) blur-only validation for larger textareas, (3) immediate soft errors on mobile for required fields.

2026-02-25 - Liam O: Drafted timing proposal: introduce a per-control 'validation-mode' token (live|debounced|onBlur) with recommended defaults: text single-line = debounced 400ms, textarea = onBlur, select = onBlur, toggle = immediate. Added note to avoid showing red 'hard' error while user is typing unless a server-side canonical value indicates a critical failure.
2026-03-02 - PM review (Sofia Nguyen): Agreed on defaults but requested an exception for inline password strength meters where live feedback is necessary. Added to scope as explicit exception.

2026-03-04 - Accessibility review (Rahul Patel): Suggested explicit SR behavior: when inline field-level error appears, announce concise text using aria-live polite; when form-level error summary appears, use role=alert and focus management pattern to avoid interrupting typing flow.

Also raised question about token naming collisions with existing semantic tokens (eg. color.error-strong vs color.error-soft).

decisions: Adopt three validation-modes at the design-system level: live (immediate), debounced (default for short text inputs, recommended 400ms), onBlur (default for textareas and selects).
Introduce two error semantic tiers: soft-error (suggestive, uses color.error-soft and 60% opacity overlay) and hard-error (blocking, uses color.error-strong).
Accessibility: field-level inline messages use aria-live=polite; form-level summary uses role=alert and focus trap pattern for keyboard users. Ensure no double announcements for same message.
Mobile behavior: reduce debounce on mobile and increase touch hit targets to 44px minimum for inputs/toggles.
